Subject: Observability billing — consolidate retention, traces, dashboards?

Hi Mina,

Quick question on our current billing: we look like we have three separate line items for retention, tracing, and advanced dashboards across different projects. Procurement is asking whether there is a cleaner commercial way to consolidate these under a single offering and ideally simplify forecasting for Q4.

Specifically:
- Can you map what portion of our charges are retention vs trace ingest vs dashboard seats?
- Is there a consolidated SKU or bundle you offer?
- Would Redwood consider a one-time migration credit or temporary discount to help move everything onto a unified plan if we commit to a 12-month term?

We’re nearing a renewal conversation and would rather avoid maintaining multiple invoices for the same org. Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Logistics

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability billing — consolidate retention, traces, dashboards?

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can consolidate and we have two pragmatic pathways depending on how you want to trade flexibility for unit economics. Below are options and the immediate data points I can send you.

Option 1 — Unified Ops Visibility Bundle (recommended):
- Single SKU that covers retention (archival + hot), trace ingest/retention, and advanced dashboard seats.
- Pricing: blended rate that reduces per-GB trace ingest by ~18% vs standalone line items at your current volumes.
- Good for teams who want a single invoice and steady monthly spend.

Option 2 — Commit + Migration Credit (best for lift-and-shift):
- 12-month commitment to the visibility bundle with tiered volume bands.
- One-time migration credit equal to 25% of the first 3 months of charges (applied as invoice credit) to offset migration friction.
- Waiver of the seat-surcharge for the first quarter.

What I need from you to give a firm quote: current 30-day ingest bytes for traces, average dashboard seats by product team, and retention breakdown (hot vs archive). I’ve attached a proposed pricing workbook (consolidation_pricing_v1.xlsx) and a short SOW template for how the migration would be structured.

If you’d like, Camila (our solutions lead) and Ben (pricing) can join a 30-min call to walk through the workbook and lock in the exact numbers.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Observability billing — consolidate retention, traces, dashboards?

Ben / Camila — forwarding Acme’s ask. Key asks: consolidate three line items and evaluate a migration credit. Proposed commercial in the attached workbook: 12-mo commit, 25% credit of first 3 months, waive seat surcharge for quarter. I think this is reasonable given deal stage (Pilot -> Enterprise) and projected ARR.

Questions for you:
- Ben: can we cap the migration-credit exposure? I’d propose a $100k cap so we don’t create an open-ended concession.
- Camila: any operational gotchas on the SOW side for moving multiple projects to one bundle (we’d want to preserve project-level RBAC/ingest tagging)?

If you both sign off I’ll send the formal quote + DocuSign SOW and loop in CS for the migration plan.

Thanks — Mina
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability billing — consolidate retention, traces, dashboards?

Mina — sounds fine, approve with the following constraints:
- Approve migration credit 25% x first 3 months but cap at $100,000 total credits.
- Require CSM sign-off on migration runbook before credit is applied (CSM needs to confirm the migration timeline and rollback plan).
- If actual usage in months 1–3 is >120% of forecast, credit on the incremental usage is void (we need to avoid subsidies for unforecasted surge).

Also, use a one-time internal approval code: FIN-APP-87 in the quote. I’ll cc finance on the final SOW.

Ben
